subject: Fritz Lang
hook: This scratched little film reel holds footage everyone thought was gone.
twist: The missing Metropolis footage was never hidden: the Buenos Aires museum had been on a distribution list since the 1920s, and it took someone repeatedly asking for the archive to be checked.

narration: This scratched little film reel holds footage everyone thought was gone. In nineteen twenty-seven, Fritz Lang premiered Metropolis at about two and a half hours. Soon it was trimmed, and the cuts vanished. Even careful restorations were still missing about a quarter of the film. In two thousand eight, a Buenos Aires curator pulled out reels until she found a scene nobody knew. The story goes that a collector carried a print to Argentina in nineteen twenty-eight. More than twenty minutes came back, badly scratched. In twenty ten, a restoration premiered in Berlin, nearly whole again. It was never hidden. The museum had been on a distribution list since the nineteen twenties. Someone just had to ask. Keep scratched footage, or hide the damage?

captions.instagram_caption:
A scratched little reel held footage everyone thought was gone. 🎞️

Fritz Lang premiered Metropolis in 1927 at about two and a half hours. Soon it was trimmed, and for decades the cut scenes could not be seen. Even careful restorations were missing about a quarter of the film.

In 2008 a curator at the Museo del Cine in Buenos Aires pulled out old reels until she found a scene nobody knew. The story goes that a collector carried a print to Argentina in 1928. More than twenty minutes came back, badly scratched.

A restored version premiered in Berlin in 2010. The restorers kept the scratched shots rather than dropping them.

The twist: it was never hidden. The museum had been on a distribution list since the 1920s. Someone just had to ask.
